root_cause.text: The TCP secure_seq code regressed timestamp offset generation to a per-host value based only on source/destination IPs, omitting TCP ports, which made TS offsets predictable across ports and enabled SYN-cookie side-channel leakage of the source port.
root_cause.evidence: The commit explicitly says it “reverts 28ee1b746f49 (‘secure_seq: downgrade to per-host timestamp offsets’)” because “off-path TCP source port leakage via SYN cookie side-channel” can be fixed by “bring[ing] back TCP ports in TS offset randomization,” and the patch changes `secure_tcp_ts_off()`/`secure_tcpv6_ts_off()` from hashing only addresses to `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off()`/`secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off()` that hash addresses plus `sport` and `dport`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The TCP secure_seq code regressed timestamp offset generation to a per-host value based only on source/destination IPs, omitting TCP ports, which made TS offsets predictable across ports and enabled SYN-cookie side-channel leakage of the source port.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit explicitly says it “reverts 28ee1b746f49 (‘secure_seq: downgrade to per-host timestamp offsets’)” because “off-path TCP source port leakage via SYN cookie side-channel” can be fixed by “bring[ing] back TCP ports in TS offset randomization,” and the patch changes `secure_tcp_ts_off()`/`secure_tcpv6_ts_off()` from hashing only addresses to `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off()`/`secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off()` that hash addresses plus `sport` and `dport`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor TCP secure sequence interfaces to return sequence and timestamp offset together with namespace-aware helpers while preserving existing sequence-only callers through inline wrappers.
intent_record.what: The header adds an extern declaration for init_net, introduces a new union tcp_seq_and_ts_off containing seq, ts_off, and a combined hash64 view, removes the separate declarations of secure_tcp_seq(), secure_tcp_ts_off(), secure_tcpv6_seq(), and secure_tcpv6_ts_off(), adds new declarations for secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off() and secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off() that take a struct net pointer and return the union, and reintroduces secure_tcp_seq() and secure_tcpv6_seq() as static inline wrappers that call the new combined functions with &init_net and return only the seq field.
intent_record.how: At runtime, IPv4 and IPv6 TCP sequence generation is routed through new combined helper functions that can compute both the TCP sequence number and timestamp offset together and with an explicit network namespace context, while existing callers of secure_tcp_seq() and secure_tcpv6_seq() still receive just the sequence number via compatibility wrappers using the initial network namespace. This enables unified derivation of both values and namespace-aware handling without breaking existing sequence-only call sites.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the secure sequence header so the file can correctly compile against secure sequence number networking interfaces.
intent_record.what: A new header include directive, `#include <net/secure_seq.h>`, was added to the file alongside the existing networking-related includes.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations from `secure_seq.h` available during compilation, enabling the file to use secure sequence number interfaces or definitions without implicit declarations or missing symbol build errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Merge separate TCP initial sequence and timestamp offset callbacks into a single combined tcp_request_sock_ops hook.
intent_record.what: The tcp_request_sock_ops struct interface was changed by removing two separate function pointers, init_seq(const struct sk_buff *skb) and init_ts_off(const struct net *net, const struct sk_buff *skb), and replacing them with a single function pointer init_seq_and_ts_off(const struct net *net, const struct sk_buff *skb) that returns a union tcp_seq_and_ts_off.
intent_record.how: At runtime, implementations of tcp_request_sock_ops will now compute and return the initial TCP sequence value and timestamp offset together through one callback instead of two separate calls. This changes the interface for callers and implementers, likely consolidating related initialization logic into a single operation rather than invoking independent functions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused ts_secret static key declaration to eliminate dead state in the module.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the file-scope declaration of a static variable named ts_secret of type siphash_aligned_key_t, while leaving the existing static net_secret declaration unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates a separate static secret key object from this compilation unit, so any behavior depending on ts_secret is no longer supported here; if the variable was unused, the practical effect is removing dead state and avoiding an unnecessary private secret allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the redundant ts_secret_init helper that wrapped ts_secret random initialization.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the static __always_inline function ts_secret_init(), including its body that called net_get_random_once(&ts_secret, sizeof(ts_secret)).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates a dedicated initializer wrapper for ts_secret, so this helper can no longer be called; behavior only changes if callers existed and are being removed or replaced elsewhere, indicating cleanup of unused or redundant initialization code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Merge IPv6 TCP sequence and timestamp-offset generation into a single net-aware helper and remove the separate timestamp-offset function.
intent_record.what: The separate IPv6 function secure_tcpv6_ts_off(const struct net *net, const __be32 *saddr, const __be32 *daddr), including its local combined-address struct, tcp_timestamps sysctl check, siphash-based timestamp offset computation, and EXPORT_IPV6_MOD declaration, was removed. The IPv6 sequence function signature was changed from u32 secure_tcpv6_seq(const __be32 *saddr, const __be32 *daddr, __be16 sport, __be16 dport) to union tcp_seq_and_ts_off secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off(const struct net *net, const __be32 *saddr, const __be32 *daddr, __be16 sport, __be16 dport).
intent_record.how: This consolidates IPv6 TCP initial sequence number and timestamp-offset handling into a single API that now also receives the network namespace, allowing one call to produce both values instead of using a separate timestamp-offset helper. It removes the standalone exported timestamp-offset entry point and shifts timestamp-related logic into the combined function path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend the IPv6 secure TCP sequence generator to return both the initial sequence number and timestamp offset, masking out the offset when TCP timestamps are disabled.
intent_record.what: The function previously returning a u32 TCP sequence hash now declares a union tcp_seq_and_ts_off variable, stores the 64-bit siphash result into its hash64 field, conditionally clears its ts_off field when net->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_timestamps is not 1, scales its seq field with seq_scale(), returns the union value instead of a u32, and updates the exported symbol name from secure_tcpv6_seq to secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now produces both an initial TCP sequence number and a timestamp offset derived from the same siphash value, while disabling the timestamp offset when TCP timestamps are not enabled; this extends the API and behavior from sequence generation only to combined sequence-and-timestamp-offset generation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Combine TCP sequence number and timestamp offset generation into one helper that returns both values while preserving timestamp-disable behavior.
intent_record.what: The patch removes the separate secure_tcp_ts_off() function and replaces secure_tcp_seq() with a new secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off() function that now takes a struct net pointer, builds a combined ports u32, computes a hash into a union tcp_seq_and_ts_off via siphash_3u32(), conditionally sets ts_off to 0 when tcp timestamps are disabled, scales the seq field with seq_scale(), returns the union, and updates the exported GPL symbol name accordingly.
intent_record.how: At runtime, TCP sequence generation and timestamp offset derivation are consolidated into a single helper that produces both values from one hash computation. This avoids a separate timestamp-offset path, preserves disabling of timestamp offsets when sysctl_tcp_timestamps is not enabled, and changes callers to receive both the initial sequence number and timestamp offset together.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the combined per-connection sequence/timestamp offset keyed by IPs and ports when adjusting TCP timestamp echoes during SYN cookie checks.
intent_record.what: Within cookie_tcp_check(), the code that computed tsoff using secure_tcp_ts_off(net, ip_hdr(skb)->daddr, ip_hdr(skb)->saddr) was replaced by declaration of a union tcp_seq_and_ts_off variable, a call to secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off(net, ip_hdr(skb)->daddr, ip_hdr(skb)->saddr, tcp_hdr(skb)->dest, tcp_hdr(skb)->source), and assignment of tsoff from st.ts_off before subtracting it from tcp_opt.rcv_tsecr.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the TCP timestamp offset used for SYN cookie validation is now derived from both IP addresses and TCP ports rather than only the addresses, using the combined sequence/timestamp offset helper and then extracting the timestamp component. This changes the computed tsecr adjustment and fixes validation behavior so timestamp handling is tied to the full 4-tuple, reducing incorrect matches across connections that share addresses but differ by ports.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add local `tcp_seq_and_ts_off` state storage in `tcp_conn_request()` to support upcoming sequence/timestamp offset handling logic.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration, `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off st;`, was added to `tcp_conn_request()` immediately after the existing `fastopen_sk` declaration.
intent_record.how: At runtime this introduces storage for a `tcp_seq_and_ts_off` union within `tcp_conn_request()`, enabling subsequent code in the function to hold sequence/timestamp-offset related state; in this diff alone it does not show direct behavioral change but prepares the function for needed logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize sequence and timestamp offset together during TCP connection request setup so the request reuses the computed timestamp offset and gets consistent state initialization.
intent_record.what: The change adds a conditional call to af_ops->init_seq_and_ts_off(net, skb) before the timestamp block when either tmp_opt.tstamp_ok is true or both !want_cookie and !isn are true, stores the result in st, and replaces the previous direct call to af_ops->init_ts_off(net, skb) with use of st.ts_off when assigning tcp_rsk(req)->ts_off.
intent_record.how: At runtime, sequence/timestamp offset initialization is now performed once through a combined helper in cases where timestamping is enabled or a non-cookie/non-ISN path needs sequence initialization, allowing the computed timestamp offset to be reused instead of independently initializing only the timestamp offset. This ensures the relevant sequence and timestamp state is prepared consistently for SYN request handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the already determined sequence number from `st.seq` in `tcp_conn_request()` to keep SYN sequence handling consistent.
intent_record.what: The code replaces the assignment of `isn` from `af_ops->init_seq(skb)` with an assignment from `st.seq` inside `tcp_conn_request()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the initial sequence number used for the connection request is now taken from the previously computed or stored `st.seq` value instead of recalculating it through `af_ops->init_seq(skb)`, which avoids using a different or inconsistent sequence source in this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Combine IPv4 TCP initial sequence and timestamp-offset initialization into a single helper that computes both values together.
intent_record.what: The diff removes two separate static helper functions, `tcp_v4_init_seq(const struct sk_buff *skb)` and `tcp_v4_init_ts_off(const struct net *net, const struct sk_buff *skb)`, and replaces them with a single static helper `tcp_v4_init_seq_and_ts_off(const struct net *net, const struct sk_buff *skb)` that returns `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off` and calls `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off(...)` with the IPv4 source/destination addresses and TCP source/destination ports.
intent_record.how: At runtime, initialization of the TCP initial sequence value and timestamp offset for IPv4 now comes from one combined computation instead of two separate helper calls. This enables both values to be derived together through `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off`, likely keeping them coordinated and avoiding duplicate per-packet extraction and separate secure function invocations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a combined helper to compute TCP initial sequence and timestamp offset together during IPv4 connect.
intent_record.what: The code in tcp_v4_connect() replaces separate calls to secure_tcp_seq() and secure_tcp_ts_off() with a single call to secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off(), storing the result in a new local variable of type union tcp_seq_and_ts_off named st, and then assigns st.seq to tp->write_seq and st.ts_off to tp->tsoffset.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the initial TCP write sequence number and timestamp offset are now derived together from one combined helper instead of being generated independently by two helpers, preserving the existing conditional behavior for tp->write_seq while updating tp->tsoffset from the combined result.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch IPv4 TCP request socket ops from separate sequence and timestamp initialization callbacks to a single combined initializer.
intent_record.what: In the tcp_request_sock_ipv4_ops structure initializer, the separate .init_seq = tcp_v4_init_seq and .init_ts_off = tcp_v4_init_ts_off assignments were removed and replaced with a single .init_seq_and_ts_off = tcp_v4_init_seq_and_ts_off assignment.
intent_record.how: At runtime, IPv4 TCP request sockets will now use one combined callback to initialize both the initial sequence number and timestamp offset instead of invoking two distinct operation hooks, aligning behavior with an interface that computes these values together.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the combined IPv6 sequence/timestamp helper with source and destination ports so syncookie timestamp offsets are computed from the full connection tuple.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a call to secure_tcpv6_ts_off() with a local union tcp_seq_and_ts_off variable initialized by secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off(), adds TCP destination and source ports as new arguments to that helper, and then assigns tsoff from st.ts_off before subtracting it from tcp_opt.rcv_tsecr.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the timestamp offset used to validate or decode the echoed TCP timestamp for IPv6 syncookies is now derived from both the IPv6 addresses and the TCP ports instead of only the addresses, producing a more specific offset value and correcting timestamp reconstruction for the connection tuple.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor TCP/IPv6 connection setup to compute the initial sequence number and timestamp offset through a single combined helper.
intent_record.what: The diff removes two separate helper functions, `tcp_v6_init_seq()` returning `u32` and `tcp_v6_init_ts_off()` returning `u32`, and replaces them with a single helper function `tcp_v6_init_seq_and_ts_off()` returning `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off`. The new function takes both `const struct net *net` and `const struct sk_buff *skb` and calls `secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off()` with the IPv6 source/destination addresses and TCP source/destination ports.
intent_record.how: At runtime, TCP/IPv6 initial sequence number generation and timestamp offset derivation are now obtained through one combined call instead of two separate calls. This enables both values to be computed together from the same inputs, which can support consistent paired generation and reduce duplicated helper logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Compute IPv6 TCP initial sequence number and timestamp offset together during connect setup to keep them consistent and correctly initialize connection state.
intent_record.what: The code in tcp_v6_connect() replaces separate calls to secure_tcpv6_seq() and secure_tcpv6_ts_off() with a single call to secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off(), storing the result in a new local variable of type union tcp_seq_and_ts_off and then assigning st.seq to tp->write_seq and st.ts_off to tp->tsoffset.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the initial TCP write sequence number and timestamp offset for an IPv6 connection are now derived together from one combined helper instead of being computed independently. This ensures both values come from the same generated state and may avoid inconsistency or duplicated work during connection setup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace separate IPv6 TCP sequence and timestamp offset initialization callbacks with a single combined request-socket operation.
intent_record.what: In the tcp_request_sock_ipv6_ops struct initializer, the separate function pointer assignments for .init_seq = tcp_v6_init_seq and .init_ts_off = tcp_v6_init_ts_off were removed and replaced with a single assignment .init_seq_and_ts_off = tcp_v6_init_seq_and_ts_off.
intent_record.how: At runtime, IPv6 TCP request socket operations will now use one combined callback to initialize both the initial sequence value and the timestamp offset instead of invoking two distinct callbacks, aligning the implementation with an updated ops interface and consolidating the initialization behavior.

consistency_review.core_intent: Unify TCP initial sequence number and timestamp offset generation/initialization for IPv4 and IPv6 by introducing combined helpers and request-socket callbacks while keeping compatibility wrappers where needed.
Remove obsolete ts_secret-related initialization and state by deleting the redundant helper and its unused backing variable.
Introduce combined TCP initial-sequence and timestamp-offset handling across connection setup by propagating sequence-plus-timestamp-offset state into SYN cookie/connection request logic.

Unify TCP sequence number and timestamp offset initialization/usage so connection setup, SYN handling, and SYN cookie timestamp validation reuse the same per-connection state consistently across IPv4 and IPv6 paths.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is specifically about TCP timestamp offset generation logic regressing in secure_seq. This group directly refactors and unifies the sequence-number and timestamp-offset generation paths for IPv4/IPv6 and request sockets, which is the same code area and mechanism implicated by the root cause, not an unrelated cleanup.

The change only adds a header include for compilation against secure sequence interfaces; it does not modify timestamp offset generation logic, hashing inputs, or TCP port inclusion related to the vulnerability root cause.

This group only removes obsolete ts_secret initialization code and unused state. The vulnerability root cause is the timestamp offset being generated without including TCP ports; deleting dead ts_secret helpers does not address or stem from that logic change.

The vulnerability is specifically about incorrect TCP timestamp-offset generation and its use during SYN-cookie/connection setup. These changes propagate combined initial-sequence plus timestamp-offset state into IPv6 secure sequence generation and tcp_conn_request()/SYN-cookie logic, directly addressing the timestamp-offset handling involved in the root cause.

The changes directly address the root cause by switching timestamp offset handling to shared per-connection state tied to the same sequence initialization path, including SYN/SYN-cookie validation and IPv4/IPv6 setup. This is aimed at restoring consistent per-connection behavior rather than a per-host IP-only timestamp offset, which is what made offsets predictable across ports.
This change directly fixes the root cause by restoring port-dependent TCP timestamp offset generation for IPv6 syncookies, using the full connection tuple instead of only IP addresses.
